request.system:
You are an extraction engine for transcripts of the Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central launch event videos.
You read machine-generated captions that carry a timestamp (seconds) per segment and you return structured JSON.

Hard rules:
- Use only what the transcript says. Do not add product knowledge, context or guesses from outside the transcript.
- Every timestamp you return must be a segment start time "t" that exists in the input, or lie inside a segment's range. Never invent timestamps.
- Quotes must be verbatim substrings of a segment text (same words, same order; you may trim the start and end). 8 to 25 words each. No paraphrasing, no fixing grammar, no stitching segments.
- Status is only what is said or shown in this video: "preview" if they say preview, public preview, beta or similar; "ga" if they say generally available, GA, out of preview, released; "announced" if it is mentioned as coming later, not in this release, roadmap; "unclear" if nothing is said. Always give the quote that proves the status, or null.
- Names of presenters are "as heard"; mark confidence low when the captions could have mangled them.
- No em-dashes anywhere in your text. Use a plain hyphen.
- Write summaries in plain language, no hype words copied from the video (no "exciting", "powerful", "seamless").

output.summary: This video covers approval process changes in Expense Agent for 2026 wave 2. It starts with AI-driven approval policies, which an admin enables and configures per expense category. It then demos the approval history and audit trail in both the Expense Agent web app and Business Central. The last part lists approval features planned for the November minor update: interim approvers, better messages, approval limits, and ad hoc and planned alternate approvers. It ends with a short mention of travel request approval.

chapters.title: Approval history and audit trail in the web app

features.name: AI-driven approval policies
features.description: An admin enables AI-driven approval policies in setup, and expense policies are configured per expense category. AI is used only for lines in categories that have a policy, and it flags expenses for approvers before final approval.
caveats: Can cause extra spending of AI tokens
Flags do not block approvers, who can still approve a flagged expense
A separate session covers this topic in depth
prerequisites: Expense policies configured per expense category

features.name: Manual compliance check by submitters
features.description: Employees who submit expenses can run the policy check manually to see in advance whether their expense is compliant. It is not run automatically for submitters.

features.name: Approval history and audit trail in the Expense Agent web app
features.description: The web app shows extra tabs (draft, submitted, approved, history, plus my approval and approve history for approvers). The history lists each step with timestamps, approver name and rejection justification, and tracks amount changes. After posting, entries by a Business Central user appear in a different color.
caveats: Posting requires a Business Central user, so posted entries show the Business Central username
prerequisites: Expense user to see the history in the web app

features.name: Approval history in Business Central
features.description: The same history is shown inside the Business Central expense report and posted expense report. It is visible to Business Central users such as accountants with rights to open the app.
caveats: An expense report that was never submitted shows no history
prerequisites: Business Central user with rights to open the app

features.name: Interim approvers
features.description: An interim approver, such as an accountant, can be added to an expense report to check it for compliance before the final approver. The interim approver must approve before the final approver.
features.status_evidence_quote: from next minor from November in some situations, you need more approvers
caveats: More approval options are planned for the future

features.name: Better messaging during approval process
features.description: Approve and reject actions show different messages, icons and colors, which makes the approval workflow easier to work with.
features.status_evidence_quote: some other approvals again uh coming from uh November 29.1

features.name: Approval limits
features.description: An approver can be given a maximum approval amount, for example $2,000, alongside an unlimited approver. Only one specific-amount level plus an unlimited level is supported.
features.status_evidence_quote: from uh November uh minor, you will be able to set up approver
caveats: An unlimited approver must be defined as the next in charge

features.name: Ad hoc alternate approver
features.description: An approver, for example on sick leave, can delegate expense reports already sent to them to a colleague. All pending expense reports are redirected to that colleague.
features.status_evidence_quote: this is what how we will have about alternate and delegated approvers from November
caveats: Alternate approvers must already be set up as approvers
prerequisites: Alternate is set up as an approver

features.name: Planned alternate approver
features.description: An approver can plan an alternate for a date range, for example October 1st to the end of October. The system automatically redirects expense reports to the chosen alternate in that period.
features.status_evidence_quote: this is what how we will have about alternate and delegated approvers from November
prerequisites: Alternate is set up as an approver

features.name: Travel request approval
features.description: Approval is being added for travel requests. Details are in a separate travel request session.
caveats: Covered only briefly, see the separate travel request session
